title: Project list Team column is sourced from the real ProjectMember join, not the removed embedded project.team field
description: Regression guard for T19/PROJECT_LEVEL_ACCESS_CONTROL: an earlier version rendered the Team column from an embedded `project.team` field that never actually existed on the backend Project schema, so it always showed 'No team'. It now reads teamPreview/teamCount, populated server-side by listByOrg's batched ProjectMember query.
steps: Open the project list and locate this project's row
expectedResult: The Team column shows an AvatarGroup with 2 avatars and a tooltip reading '2 team members' — it must never regress to showing 'No team' for a project that genuinely has members.

title: After a project-list refresh, the selected project defaults to one the user administers rather than an arbitrary first entry
description: Regression guard for RBAC-01: projectSlice's fetchProjects.fulfilled reducer prefers `list.find(p => p.isProjectRoleAdmin) || list[0]` both on first load and when the previously-selected project no longer exists in the refreshed list — never falls back to a plain member project when an admin one is available.
preconditions: User is a plain Member on Project A and the per-project admin on Project B; Project A happens to sort before Project B in the fetched list
steps: Log in fresh (no prior selectedProject in state) and observe which project ProjectSelector defaults to
Get removed from Project A's membership by another admin, then trigger a projects refetch (e.g. reload)
expectedResult: In both cases, ProjectSelector defaults to Project B (the one this user administers), never to Project A merely because it appears first in the array.

title: Updating only extraPermissions for a team member must not silently reset their projectRoleId to null (and vice versa)
description: updateTeamMemberRole (project.controller.js) builds setFields conditionally: `if (projectRoleId !== undefined) ... if (validatedPermissions !== undefined) ...` — only touching a field the caller actually sent. A prior/naive implementation could have applied both fields unconditionally, wiping out whichever one wasn't included in a given request body.
preconditions: A ProjectMember has projectRoleId set to the 'Auditor' Custom Project Role and extraPermissions ['evidence.approve']
steps: Call PUT /projects/project/:id/team/:userId with body { extraPermissions: ['evidence.approve', 'risk.read'] } only (no projectRoleId field at all)
expectedResult: The member's projectRoleId is still 'Auditor' (unchanged) and extraPermissions now includes both entries — the omitted field was never touched, matching the documented 'both fields independently optional' contract.

title: Re-adding an existing project team member returns a friendly 409 conflict, not a duplicate row or a 500 crash
description: The unique index on {projectId, userId} (ProjectMember schema) means a second addTeamMember call for the same pair throws a Mongo 11000 error, which the controller specifically catches and rethrows as AppError.conflict('User is already a member of this project') — 'a friendly no-op, not a crash or a duplicate row (T4 acceptance criteria).'
preconditions: userId U is already a ProjectMember of Project X
steps: As a Project X admin, call POST /api/projects/project/:X_id/team with { userId: U } a second time
expectedResult: Response is 409 with message 'User is already a member of this project' — no second ProjectMember row is created, and the endpoint does not surface a raw 500/duplicate-key error to the caller.

title: A user removed from a project's ProjectSelector list no longer sees that project's data on a subsequent module-page load
description: projectSlice's fetchProjects.fulfilled reducer validates the persisted selectedProject still exists in the freshly fetched list; if not, it clears/reassigns rather than leaving a stale selectedProject object (with stale permissions) in memory after a membership change.
preconditions: User currently has Project X selected and is viewing Evidence Management scoped to it; an admin then removes the user from Project X's team
steps: With Project X selected, trigger any action that refetches the project list (e.g. navigating between pages that call initializeProjects, or a manual refresh)
Observe the ProjectSelector and any project-scoped module page
expectedResult: Project X no longer appears in the selector's list; selectedProject is reassigned to another project the user still belongs to (or cleared to null if none remain) — Project X's evidence/risk/audit data is not shown under any subsequently selected context.
